1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Pellmore Software sells Crewlane, a subscription scheduling and invoicing tool for small trades businesses such as plumbers, electricians and heating engineers. About 9,400 accounts were active at the end of March 2026. Crewlane connects to two accounting packages, Quillbook and Tallymarsh. On 1 April 2026 Pellmore raised the Standard list price. Around 2,100 'Founders' accounts kept a price lock from a 2025 campaign. Monthly cancellations rose soon after the increase. Stage S1 covers late May to early June 2026, when the finance team first analysed the rise. Stage S2 is mid-August 2026.
9	Your request: The CEO wants a recommendation before the 2 September board meeting. Is the rise in cancellations a pricing problem? Should the April increase be reversed? What else, if anything, should Pellmore do now?
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Memo from Dana Okafor, CFO, to the executive team, 8 June 2026 (leadership-account): Re: April–May churn. Monthly logo churn was 2.4% in April and 2.8% in May, against 1.8% in Q1. Those are the first two months after the Standard list price moved from $39 to $49 per seat. Exit surveys name price as the top reason. Account managers report price pushback on most renewal calls. The finance cut also shows that the bigger an account's dollar increase, the more likely it was to leave. This is a pricing problem. I recommend we prepare a rollback of the increase for repriced accounts and offer targeted retention discounts in the meantime. Every month we wait costs us more of the base.
12	- Cancellation-flow survey export, customer success operations (system-record): Cancellation-flow survey, 1 April–31 May 2026. Respondents: 396 of 484 cancelling accounts (82%). Question: 'What is the main reason you are leaving?' (single choice). Price / not worth the cost: 194 (49%). Moving to another product: 67 (17%). Business closed or seasonal: 44 (11%). Missing feature: 32 (8%). Product problems or bugs: 28 (7%). Other: 31 (8%). Q1 2026 comparison (291 respondents): Price / not worth the cost 31%, Moving to another product 15%, Business closed or seasonal 24%, Missing feature 12%, Product problems or bugs 6%, Other 12%.
13	- Finance team analysis, prepared 5 June 2026 (financial-record): Cancellations by account size, April–May 2026. Repriced accounts only (Founders excluded); increase = seats × $10. Average seats: cancelled repriced accounts 5.0, active repriced base 3.3. Average monthly increase at the new list price: cancelled accounts $50, active repriced base $33. Monthly churn by seat band, repriced accounts: 1–2 seats 2.0% (Q1 1.8%); 3–5 seats 2.7% (Q1 1.8%); 6+ seats 3.9% (Q1 1.9%). Analyst comment: 'Clear dose-response. Repriced accounts facing the largest dollar increase left at about twice their Q1 rate, while the smallest barely moved.'
14	- Weekly support note, Priya Nand, support lead, 29 May 2026 (manager-account): April–May ticket volume is up 31% on Q1, with headcount unchanged at 14 agents. Mobile 5.0 layout complaints peaked in the first week of April and have mostly faded since the 5.0.2 patch. 'Accounting sync' tickets (Quillbook and Tallymarsh share the tag) went from about 30 to about 70 a week. Most are about invoices missing or doubled at month-end. A manual re-sync works, so they are logged Sev-3 and escalate to Tier 2. Median first response rose from 6 to 19 hours. Accounts that cancelled in May had a median first response of 26 hours on their last ticket, against 7 hours for active accounts that raised tickets.
15	- Revenue operations reference sheet, as of 31 May 2026 (system-record): Monthly logo churn, April–July average: 2024 1.7%, 2025 1.9%. Q1 2026: 1.8%. April 2026: 2.4%. May 2026: 2.8%. Active accounts at 31 March 2026: 9,400. Change calendar: 24 March, mobile app 5.0 (forced update to all accounts); 1 April, Standard list price raised from $39 to $49 per seat for repriced accounts. About 2,100 'Founders' accounts hold a price lock at $39 until 31 December 2026. Accounting connectors in use: Quillbook (about 1,900 accounts) and Tallymarsh (about 300).
16	- Email from Marcus Lindqvist, CEO, to the executive team, 12 August 2026 (leadership-account): Churn was 3.0% in June and 3.1% in July. The retention offer (20% off for six months to accounts the health score flagged, from 15 June) has not moved the total. Dana wants to return all repriced accounts to $39 from 1 September, roughly $220k a month in revenue, because she thinks the offer was too narrow. Tomas (product) says 'sync paused' is now the commonest phrase in tickets and wants the duplicate-invoice hold switched off so syncs run through. Ines (engineering) proposes that a separate two-person team rebuild the Tallymarsh connector over six weeks in case it is affected too. That work would not touch anything else. The board meets 2 September and I need a recommendation.
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from Quillbook invoice-sync failures that began when Quillbook retired its old interface on 30 March. Accounts with no connector, repriced or not, barely moved (1.8% to 1.9%). Quillbook accounts rose from about 2% to about 6%, whether or not they had the price lock. Of the 1,212 Quillbook accounts that had sync failures, 34% cancelled, against 8% of those with none. The failures are logged as warnings, so the health panel misses them. The price-size pattern in the finance analysis is explained by larger accounts being more likely to use Quillbook. Tallymarsh changes are too small to tell apart from normal variation. I'm fairly confident, around 85–90%.
20	
21	Recommendation:
22	- Don't roll back the price. It would cost about $220k a month and would not address the cause.
23	- Don't switch off the duplicate-invoice hold. It protects customers' books.
24	- Make the Quillbook fix (move to v3, three to four weeks) the top engineering priority.
25	- Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct invoices.
26	- Review the Tallymarsh log before committing a rebuild team.
27	- Make sync failures visible on the health panel and speed up support response to sync tickets.
28
